question: A 42-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 10-month history of joint pain and stiffness in her wrists and fingers. The symptoms are worse in the morning and improve with activity. Physical examination shows swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints in both hands. An x-ray of the hands is shown. Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Joint pain and stiffness in wrists and fingers" -> "Worse in the morning, improves with activity" -> "Swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints in both hands" -> "Likely inflammatory arthritis" -> "Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show inflammation" -> "Monosodium urate crystals" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Joint pain and stiffness in wrists and fingers" -> "Worse in the morning, improves with activity" -> "Swelling and warmth over MCP and wrist joints in both hands" -> "Likely inflammatory arthritis" -> "Synovial biopsy from an affected joint would most likely show inflammation" -> "Calcium pyrophosphate crystals" -> 80%
analysis: The clinical presentation of joint pain and stiffness in the wrists and fingers, along with swelling and warmth over the MCP and wrist joints, is suggestive of inflammatory arthritis. Given the symptoms and findings, the most likely finding on synovial biopsy would be the presence of monosodium urate crystals, indicating gout as the underlying cause.
